title: Finite-projective point dual and tensor models
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $A_m=(R/\varpi^m)_s$ for $m\ge1$ and $B=\varprojlim_m A_m$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and put $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; apply $L$ and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes.
Assume $R$ is Noetherian, $L$ and $\Gamma$ are exact, $R\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma B$ is the constant-value map, and $L\dashv\Gamma$ has bijection $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h_s(1\otimes x))$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes x\mapsto b\,t(x)|_U)$. Let $P$ be a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Put $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$, with differential $d(f)=-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_P$ [def-pur-hom-complex], $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RP^\vee)$, $C=L(P)$, $J=L(P^\vee)$ and $D=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_BJ)$, with signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then $P^\vee,T$ are bounded finite-projective complexes, and $P,P^\vee,T$ have finitely generated cohomology and are K-flat over $R$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Each term of $C,J,D$ is a summand of a finite sum of $B$; these complexes are bounded flat-term K-flat models [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The balancing map $(b\otimes x)\otimes(b'\otimes f)\mapsto bb'\otimes(x\otimes f)$ gives $D\cong L(T)$, representing $C\otimes_B^LJ$. The four complexes $B[0],C,J,D$ belong to $D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and have finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with one bound for every finite reduction. The adjunction units of $R[0],P,P^\vee,T$ are quasi-isomorphisms, with their actual formula $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ (and $r\mapsto r$ for $R$).
The chain map $J\to\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(C,B[0])$ sends $b\otimes f$ to $(b'\otimes x\mapsto bb'f(x))$ and is an isomorphism. Through the canonical ordinary-Hom-to-derived-Hom map, it induces the canonical isomorphism $J\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

proof.text: Use the explicit finite-support degree isomorphisms for the scalar dual and total tensor. For each of P, its dual, and its tensor, cycles are finite as submodules of finite modules over the Noetherian ring, and homology is their quotient. Projective terms are flat; bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat.

Apply the normalized finite-projective extension-model theorem separately to P, its dual, and its scalar total tensor. The displayed finite-free splittings give site-flatness and independent-universe K-flatness. Apply the K-flat total tensor theorem to the first two models.

Use the normalized total tensor comparison. Transport the bounds and finite-free retractions of L(T) along its inverse to the actual tensor complex D. The K-flat total tensor theorem supplies its derived tensor representation.

Apply the perfect point extension constructibility theorem to P, the dual, and the scalar total tensor. It supplies B[0] as well. For D transport integral constructibility along the localized tensor comparison. For each finite reduction compose the representative isomorphism with that reduction of the comparison; this transports the same Tor interval.

Apply the explicit adjunction-unit theorem termwise. The single ring complex has finite-projective terms also away from degree zero because those terms are zero. Componentwise invertibility gives an isomorphism of complexes, hence a quasi-isomorphism. Keep the generator formula and normalized rank-one coefficient isomorphism furnished by that theorem.

Use the normalized ordinary finite-projective dual comparison. For the canonical derived-Hom map, each term of C is a displayed finite-free retract; internal Hom from it preserves short exact sequences. The bounded exact-term Hom theorem makes Hom(C,-) preserve the fixed K-injective-resolution quasi-isomorphism. Its localized map and the defining resolution comparison are isomorphisms, so composing with the localized ordinary dual comparison gives the final assertion.

proof_origin.place: T1: explicit Lean assembly of the finite-projective point argument, with normalized tensor, ordinary dual, and completed constructibility comparisons separated. Canonical derived-Hom comparison uses bounded exact terms rather than the bounded-free model theorem. B2: the unit retains its original body and records its definitionally identical concrete point-sections codomain. Proved unit_apply and unit_isIso expose its generator formula and componentwise isomorphism criterion; the original model theorem and proof are unchanged. The proved scalar_eq exposes the equality of the generic scalar map and the recorded integral point-section map. The canonical unitIso names the same asIso construction and its unitIso_apply formula is proved from unit_apply. Its inverse is uniquely determined by the unit.
